videos.author: @culturalperspective
videos.description: DOGE promised trillions in savings. What did it save? Government auditors cannot verify most of what DOGE claims. DOGE promised to cut trillions from the US government. Government auditors cannot verify most of what it says it saved. The target kept shrinking. Elon Musk first claimed 2 trillion dollars in cuts, then lowered it to 1 trillion. By July 2026, DOGE's own website claimed about 110 billion dollars. Then the Government Accountability Office checked the math. In a report dated August 6, 2026, the GAO could not verify how 96 percent of the claimed grant savings were calculated. Some of the listed savings were clerical errors. Others were contract cancellations already in motion before DOGE existed. The costs are easier to measure. The nonpartisan Partnership for Public Service estimated DOGE cost about 135 billion dollars in its first year, through firings, paid leave, and rehiring. The Yale Budget Lab projects that the IRS staff cuts alone will lose about 598 billion dollars in revenue over ten years, because fewer auditors means less tax collected. Those cost figures are estimates. The claimed savings are mostly unverified. Americans were promised that a rich businessman would run the government lean. The receipts do not add up. The measured costs are larger than the savings anyone can confirm. This is cultural programming against the ledger. The promise was simple and the audit is specific, and they point in opposite directions. Want the full breakdown of the DOGE numbers? videos.description: President Trump on Friday commended Elon Musk for his DOGE efforts as the world’s richest man prepared to depart the government to return to his companies.   “Elon has worked tirelessly, helping lead the most sweeping and consequential government reform programs in generations,” the president told reporters in the Oval Office.   Mr. Musk is leaving the government after four months of trying to shrink the federal workforce and cut spending, a period during which his companies suffered reputational and financial damage.   “He willingly accepted the outrageous abuse and slander and lies and attacks because he does love our country,” the president said, adding that “Americans owe him a great debt of gratitude.”   “He had to go through the slings and the arrows, which is a shame because he’s an incredible patriot.”   Mr. Musk fell well short of his goal of eliminating $1 trillion in government spending but said the DOGE efforts would continue, calling it “a way of life.”   “This is not the end of DOGE, but really the beginning,” he said. “The DOGE team will only grow stronger over time. The DOGE influence will only go stronger.”   “I am confident that, over time, we will see a trillion dollars of savings and a reduction in — a trillion dollars of waste and fraud reduction,” he added. #elonmusk #trump #doge #cspan

videos.author: @pbsnews
videos.description: The Social Security Administration now says members of Elon Musk's DOGE team working at the agency last year accessed and shared sensitive data. In a court filing earlier this month, the Trump administration amended what it had previously disclosed, writing that one DOGE employee at SSA signed an agreement with an unnamed political advocacy group to analyze voter rolls to "find evidence of voter fraud and to overturn election results in certain states." In another instance, a DOGE member shared personally identifiable information of 1,000 people in an encrypted e-mail attachment, though the government says they aren't sure what specifically was shared or whether it was accessed. The SSA also said DOGE shared data on third-party cloud servers that were "outside SSA's security protocols," and the agency doesn't know what information was shared or if it still exists on the server. The latest disclosures seemed to confirm some key concerns first raised in a whistle-blower complaint last summer filed by Chuck Borges, the agency's chief data officer. Borges involuntarily resigned from government in August and filed a retaliation complaint late last year. For more, Geoff Bennett spoke to Borges and his lawyer, Debra Katz. #pbs #pbsnews #pbsnewshour #donaldtrump #trumpadministration #elonmusk #DOGE #SSA #socialsecurity #DOJ #whistleblower

mentions.title: President Trump on Friday commended Elon Musk for his DOGE efforts as the world’s richest man prepared to depart the government to return to his companies.   “Elon has worked tirelessly, helping lead the most sweeping and consequential government reform programs in generations,” the president told reporters in the Oval Office.   Mr. Musk is leaving the government after four months of trying to shrink the federal workforce and cut spending, a period during which his companies suffered reputational and financial damage.   “He willingly accepted the outrageous abuse and slander and lies and attacks because he does love our country,” the president said, adding that “Americans owe him a great debt of gratitude.”   “He had to go through the slings and the arrows, which is a shame because he’s an incredible patriot.”   Mr. Musk fell well short of his goal of eliminating $1 trillion in government spending but said the DOGE efforts would continue, calling it “a way of life.”   “This is not the end of DOGE, but really the beginning,” he said. “The DOGE team will only grow stronger over time. The DOGE influence will only go stronger.”   “I am confident that, over time, we will see a trillion dollars of savings and a reduction in — a trillion dollars of waste and fraud reduction,” he added. #elonmusk #trump #doge #cspan

mentions.title: The Social Security Administration now says members of Elon Musk's DOGE team working at the agency last year accessed and shared sensitive data. In a court filing earlier this month, the Trump administration amended what it had previously disclosed, writing that one DOGE employee at SSA signed an agreement with an unnamed political advocacy group to analyze voter rolls to "find evidence of voter fraud and to overturn election results in certain states." In another instance, a DOGE member shared personally identifiable information of 1,000 people in an encrypted e-mail attachment, though the government says they aren't sure what specifically was shared or whether it was accessed. The SSA also said DOGE shared data on third-party cloud servers that were "outside SSA's security protocols," and the agency doesn't know what information was shared or if it still exists on the server. The latest disclosures seemed to confirm some key concerns first raised in a whistle-blower complaint last summer filed by Chuck Borges, the agency's chief data officer. Borges involuntarily resigned from government in August and filed a retaliation complaint late last year. For more, Geoff Bennett spoke to Borges and his lawyer, Debra Katz. #pbs #pbsnews #pbsnewshour #donaldtrump #trumpadministration #elonmusk #DOGE #SSA #socialsecurity #DOJ #whistleblower
